explainTr: Bir kelimeyi bilmek, ailesini bilmek demektir. Fiil + -tion/-ment/-ance → isim (educate → education, improve → improvement, assist → assistance). Isim/fiil + -ful/-ive/-able/-al → sıfat (help → helpful, create → creative, rely → reliable). Sıfat + -ly → zarf (careful → carefully).

Ön ekler anlamı değiştirir: un-, in-, im-, dis- çoğunlukla zıt anlam verir (unclear, inflexible, impossible, disagree). Kural: p/b/m öncesinde im- (impossible), l öncesinde il-, r öncesinde ir-. Sınavda boşluğa bakıp 'burada isim mi, sıfat mı, zarf mı?' diye sor.
Kelimeleri tek başına değil, birlikte öğren: make a decision, pay attention, give a presentation. Phrasal verb'ler de blok olarak öğrenilir: go over, call off, come up with.
grammar.compareTr: Türkçe de ek ile kelime türetir (göz → gözlük → gözlükçü). İngilizce aynı mantıktadır ama ekler başa da gelir: un-happy. Türkçeden farklı olarak kelimenin türü değişince biçimi de değişir ve cümledeki yeri belirler.

reading.title: A job posting full of new words
reading.text:
Hafsa found a job posting for a long-term substitute position at Roosevelt Middle School. She read it slowly: "We are looking for a flexible and enthusiastic teacher who can collaborate with our staff. Applicants must show strong communication skills, creativity, and the ability to organize a productive classroom."

She underlined six words she did not know. Then she remembered a trick from her English class: look at the word, not the whole sentence. For example, "enthusiastic" must be related to "enthusiasm," a noun she had heard before. "Flexible" reminded her of "flexibility," and the prefix "in-" in "inflexible" gave her the opposite. "Communication" came from "communicate," a verb she used every day.

Emre sat down next to her. "Mom, you are using the dictionary too much," he said. "Try to guess first." Together they played a game. Emre wrote a base word on a sheet of paper, and Hafsa had to make as many related words as possible. For "create," she wrote "creative," "creativity," "creation," and "creator." For "organize," she wrote "organization" and "organized," but she forgot "disorganized." Emre gave her a point for each correct word.

"Why is this so useful?" Hafsa asked. "Because English has thousands of words that are built from the same roots," Emre said. "If you know one, you usually understand four more." Hafsa nodded slowly. It made her feel less afraid. She had worried that she would need to memorize ten thousand separate words, but now she saw that many of them were relatives.

At the end of the evening, she wrote a short cover letter. She used "flexible," "productive," and "collaborate" in the first paragraph, which made her smile. "Last year I could not read this posting," she wrote in her notebook. "Today I can answer it." The next morning she sent the application before breakfast.

script.speaker: Linda

script.speaker: Linda
script.text: Assistance is just help. It comes from the verb assist.

script.speaker: Hafsa

script.speaker: Linda
script.text: It means working together. The verb is cooperate. Words ending in -tion are usually nouns.

script.speaker: Linda
script.text: And many adjectives end in -ful or -ive, like helpful and creative. Write that in your notebook!

writing.promptEn: Write a paragraph (120-180 words) explaining how you learn word families. Give examples of base words and their related forms, and say how you will study in the future.
frames: When I see a new word, I first ...
For example, the noun ... comes from the verb ...
The prefix un- / in- / dis- gives the opposite, as in ...
writing.model:
When I see a new word, I first look at its parts instead of opening the dictionary. For example, the noun "cooperation" comes from the verb "cooperate," and the adjective "cooperative" is from the same family. If I know one word, I can usually guess two or three more.

Prefixes and suffixes are also very helpful. The prefix un- or in- often gives the opposite, as in "unclear" or "inflexible." The suffix -ful or -ive often shows an adjective, like "helpful" or "creative," while -tion and -ment usually show a noun, like "education" or "improvement."

I think this method is better than memorizing long lists because the words are connected in my mind.

In the future, I will write one word family on a card every day. I will also read the school emails slowly and underline every word I can build from a known root. If I keep doing this, I believe my vocabulary will grow much faster, and I will feel more confident in the classroom.
checklistTr: En az üç kelime ailesi örneği verdin mi (isim, fiil, sıfat)?
Bir ön ek (un-, in-, dis-) ve bir son ek (-ful, -ive, -tion) örneği var mı?
Gelecek planı için will kullandın mı?
Fikirleri bağlayan linkers kullandın mı (for example, also, because)?
